The formation of secondary cracks consumes a lot of energy during the fatigue fracture process, dispersing the stress and reducing the stress concentration at the major crack front, thus reducing the crack growth rate.

The SAGBO model was initially proposed to clarify the low expansion superalloy IN903 [10]. This indicated that the time-dependent crack propagation is ordinarily caused by oxidation of the crack tip under stress.
Liu and White [12] proposed the Dynamic Embrittlement model (DE model), also illustrated in Fig. 7, to describe the oxygen-induced cracking in Ni3Al alloy.

From the SAGBO and DE models, the decrease in the plastic zone reduces the amount of plastic deformation near the crack tip which can reduce the depth of oxidation and decrease the fatigue crack growth rate.
